Landmark Analysis at Day 30 — Sensitivity Analysis

Chen et al. 2023, Cancers 15:2521 — AE-Derived Biomarkers in NSCLC Immunotherapy

Published

November 2, 2026

Purpose. This document assesses whether the key survival associations reported in Chen et al. (2023) are affected by guarantee-time (immortal-time) bias. Because AE biomarkers are defined over the first 30 days of treatment, patients who die (or progress) before day 30 are necessarily in the “no early AE” group — which could artificially inflate the observed survival difference. A landmark analysis at day 30 addresses this by restricting both survival endpoints to patients who were still alive (or progression-free) at day 30, and measuring time-to-event from that landmark forward.

Data source. AE.dataA_correct.csv, clin.dataA_correct.csv, AE.dataB_correct.csv, clin.dataB_correct.csv.
Landmark. Day 30 from on-treatment date. OS landmark: patients with os_time > 30 days; PFS landmark: patients with pfs_time > 30 days. Survival times are shifted: os_time_lm = os_time − 30, pfs_time_lm = pfs_time − 30.

Biomarker definition is unchanged. AE biomarkers (occurrence, frequency, duration) are still computed from AEs with time_onset ≤ 30. The landmark only affects who enters the survival model and what time origin is used.

Show code 
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(survival)
library(survminer)
library(ggplot2)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(knitr)

## ── Load correctedData ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cd <- "correctedData"
clin_A   <- read_csv(file.path(cd, "clin.dataA_correct.csv"),   show_col_types = FALSE)
ae_raw_A <- read_csv(file.path(cd, "AE.dataA_correct.csv"),     show_col_types = FALSE)
clin_B   <- read_csv(file.path(cd, "clin.dataB_correct.csv"),   show_col_types = FALSE)
ae_raw_B <- read_csv(file.path(cd, "AE.dataB_correct.csv"),     show_col_types = FALSE)

## ── Landmark parameter ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
LM_DAYS <- 30
LM_MO   <- LM_DAYS / 30.4375   # ≈ 0.986 months

## ── Cohort A: survival objects ────────────────────────────────────────────────
surv_A <- clin_A |>
  mutate(
    os_time_mo   = os_time  / 30.4375,
    pfs_time_mo  = pfs_time / 30.4375,
    os_event     = os_censor,
    pfs_event    = pfs_censor,
    dot_days     = treatment.time,
    response_bin = if_else(response == "Non-PD", "DC", "PD"))

surv_A_dcpd <- surv_A |> filter(!is.na(response_bin))

## ── Cohort B: survival objects ────────────────────────────────────────────────
surv_B <- clin_B |>
  mutate(
    os_time_mo   = os_time  / 30.4375,
    pfs_time_mo  = pfs_time / 30.4375,
    os_event     = os_censor,
    pfs_event    = pfs_censor,
    dot_days     = treatment.time,
    response_bin = if_else(response == "Non-PD", "DC", "PD"))

surv_B_dcpd <- surv_B |> filter(!is.na(response_bin))

## ── Early AE objects (unchanged — biomarker definition is identical) ──────────
ae_early_A <- ae_raw_A |>
  filter(!is.na(grade)) |>
  mutate(
    early      = time_onset <= 30,
    trae       = AE_Trt == "Yes",
    low_grade  = grade %in% c(1, 2),
    high_grade = grade >= 3,
    dur_incl   = pmin(coalesce(time_resolved, 30L), 30L) - time_onset + 1L,
    ae_name    = tolower(trimws(toxicity_ind))) |>
  filter(early)

ae_early_B <- ae_raw_B |>
  filter(!is.na(grade)) |>
  mutate(
    early      = time_onset <= 30,
    trae       = AE_Trt == "Yes",
    low_grade  = grade %in% c(1, 2),
    high_grade = grade >= 3,
    dur_incl   = pmin(coalesce(time_resolved, 30L), 30L) - time_onset + 1L,
    ae_name    = tolower(trimws(toxicity_ind))) |>
  filter(early)

## ── Landmark survival objects ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
# OS landmark: patients with os_time > LM_DAYS; time measured from landmark
surv_A_lm_os  <- surv_A |>
  filter(os_time  > LM_DAYS) |>
  mutate(os_time_lm  = os_time_mo  - LM_MO,
         pfs_time_lm = pmax(pfs_time_mo - LM_MO, 0))   # PFS may have occurred before LM

# PFS landmark: patients with pfs_time > LM_DAYS
surv_A_lm_pfs <- surv_A |>
  filter(pfs_time > LM_DAYS) |>
  mutate(pfs_time_lm = pfs_time_mo - LM_MO)

# Combined landmark (patients with BOTH os_time > LM and pfs_time > LM):
# Since pfs_time <= os_time always, this equals the PFS landmark set.
surv_A_lm <- surv_A |>
  filter(pfs_time > LM_DAYS) |>
  mutate(os_time_lm  = os_time_mo  - LM_MO,
         pfs_time_lm = pfs_time_mo - LM_MO)

surv_A_lm_dcpd <- surv_A_lm |> filter(!is.na(response_bin))

surv_B_lm_os  <- surv_B |>
  filter(os_time  > LM_DAYS) |>
  mutate(os_time_lm  = os_time_mo  - LM_MO,
         pfs_time_lm = pmax(pfs_time_mo - LM_MO, 0))

surv_B_lm_pfs <- surv_B |>
  filter(pfs_time > LM_DAYS) |>
  mutate(pfs_time_lm = pfs_time_mo - LM_MO)

surv_B_lm <- surv_B |>
  filter(pfs_time > LM_DAYS) |>
  mutate(os_time_lm  = os_time_mo  - LM_MO,
         pfs_time_lm = pfs_time_mo - LM_MO)

surv_B_lm_dcpd <- surv_B_lm |> filter(!is.na(response_bin))

## ── Helper: KM stats (median + logrank p) ─────────────────────────────────────
km_stats <- function(fit, sd) {
  med <- summary(fit)$table[, "median"]
  p   <- 1 - pchisq(sd$chisq, df = 1)
  list(med = round(med, 2), p = round(p, 4))
}

## ── 24-biomarker builder (same as original) ───────────────────────────────────
build_bio24 <- function(ae_df, surv_df) {
  specs <- tribble(
    ~label,           ~grade_filter, ~trt_only,
    "High_Grade",     "high", FALSE, "High_Grade_Trt", "high", TRUE,
    "Low_Grade",      "low",  FALSE, "Low_Grade_Trt",  "low",  TRUE,
    "Any_Grade",      "any",  FALSE, "Any_Grade_Trt",  "any",  TRUE)
  build_one <- function(label, grade_filter, trt_only) {
    d <- ae_df
    if (grade_filter == "low")  d <- d |> filter(low_grade)
    if (grade_filter == "high") d <- d |> filter(high_grade)
    if (trt_only) d <- d |> filter(trae)
    d |> group_by(id) |>
      summarise(
        !!paste0(label,"_occ")  := 1L,
        !!paste0(label,"_fuq")  := n_distinct(ae_name),
        !!paste0(label,"_fall") := n(),
        !!paste0(label,"_dur")  := sum(dur_incl, na.rm=TRUE), .groups="drop")
  }
  bio <- surv_df |> select(id)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(specs)))
    bio <- bio |> left_join(
      build_one(specs$label[i], specs$grade_filter[i], specs$trt_only[i]), by = "id")
  bio |> mutate(across(-id, ~replace_na(.x, 0)))
}

## ── Landmark Cox forest ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# OS and PFS use separate landmark datasets (proper per-endpoint landmark)
cox_forest_lm <- function(bio24, surv_df, lm_mo = LM_MO) {
  bio_cols <- setdiff(names(bio24), "id")

  # Per-endpoint landmark subsets
  dat_os  <- surv_df |>
    filter(os_time_mo  > lm_mo) |>
    mutate(os_time_mo  = os_time_mo  - lm_mo) |>
    left_join(bio24, by = "id")
  dat_pfs <- surv_df |>
    filter(pfs_time_mo > lm_mo) |>
    mutate(pfs_time_mo = pfs_time_mo - lm_mo) |>
    left_join(bio24, by = "id")

  map_dfr(bio_cols, function(col) {
    tryCatch({
      cx_os  <- summary(coxph(as.formula(paste0("Surv(os_time_mo,os_event)~",  col)), data=dat_os))$coefficients
      cx_pfs <- summary(coxph(as.formula(paste0("Surv(pfs_time_mo,pfs_event)~",col)), data=dat_pfs))$coefficients
      tibble(biomarker=col,
             hr_os=exp(cx_os[1,1]),  p_os=cx_os[1,5],  n_os=nrow(dat_os),
             hr_pfs=exp(cx_pfs[1,1]),p_pfs=cx_pfs[1,5],n_pfs=nrow(dat_pfs))
    }, error=function(e) tibble(biomarker=col,hr_os=NA,p_os=NA,n_os=NA,hr_pfs=NA,p_pfs=NA,n_pfs=NA))
  }) |>
    mutate(
      category = sub("_(occ|fuq|fall|dur)$","",biomarker),
      measure  = sub(".*_(occ|fuq|fall|dur)$","\\1",biomarker),
      sig_os   = !is.na(p_os)  & p_os  < 0.05,
      sig_pfs  = !is.na(p_pfs) & p_pfs < 0.05)
}

## ── Original Cox forest (for comparison) ─────────────────────────────────────
cox_forest_orig <- function(bio24, surv_df) {
  bio_cols <- setdiff(names(bio24), "id")
  dat <- surv_df |> left_join(bio24, by = "id")
  map_dfr(bio_cols, function(col) {
    tryCatch({
      cx_os  <- summary(coxph(as.formula(paste0("Surv(os_time_mo,os_event)~",  col)), data=dat))$coefficients
      cx_pfs <- summary(coxph(as.formula(paste0("Surv(pfs_time_mo,pfs_event)~",col)), data=dat))$coefficients
      tibble(biomarker=col,
             hr_os=exp(cx_os[1,1]),  p_os=cx_os[1,5],
             hr_pfs=exp(cx_pfs[1,1]),p_pfs=cx_pfs[1,5])
    }, error=function(e) tibble(biomarker=col,hr_os=NA,p_os=NA,hr_pfs=NA,p_pfs=NA))
  }) |>
    mutate(
      category = sub("_(occ|fuq|fall|dur)$","",biomarker),
      measure  = sub(".*_(occ|fuq|fall|dur)$","\\1",biomarker),
      sig_os   = !is.na(p_os)  & p_os  < 0.05,
      sig_pfs  = !is.na(p_pfs) & p_pfs < 0.05)
}

## ── Response t-test (landmark: restrict to OS-landmark patients) ──────────────
resp_ttest_lm <- function(bio24, surv_dcpd, lm_mo = LM_MO) {
  bio_cols <- setdiff(names(bio24), "id")
  dat <- surv_dcpd |>
    filter(os_time_mo > lm_mo) |>
    left_join(bio24, by = "id")
  map_dfr(bio_cols, function(col) {
    x   <- dat[[col]]; grp <- dat$response_bin
    ok  <- !is.na(grp); x <- x[ok]; grp <- grp[ok]
    tt  <- tryCatch(t.test(x ~ grp), error=function(e) NULL)
    tibble(biomarker=col,
           mean_DC = mean(x[grp=="DC"]), mean_PD = mean(x[grp=="PD"]),
           diff    = mean(x[grp=="DC"]) - mean(x[grp=="PD"]),
           p       = if(!is.null(tt)) tt$p.value else NA_real_)
  }) |>
    mutate(
      category = sub("_(occ|fuq|fall|dur)$","",biomarker),
      measure  = sub(".*_(occ|fuq|fall|dur)$","\\1",biomarker),
      sig = !is.na(p) & p < 0.05)
}

Figure 2A/B — Low-grade TrAE vs Survival (landmark)

Paper (original): n = 22 with / 10 without; PFS p = 0.002; OS p = 0.007.

Show code 
lg_trae_occ <- ae_early_A |>
  filter(trae, low_grade) |>
  distinct(id) |> mutate(lg_trae = 1L)

## Original analysis
df_A_lg <- surv_A |>
  left_join(lg_trae_occ, by = "id") |>
  mutate(lg_trae = replace_na(lg_trae, 0L),
         group   = factor(lg_trae, levels=c(0,1), labels=c("No LG TrAE","LG TrAE")))

## Landmark analysis (OS landmark for OS, PFS landmark for PFS)
df_A_lg_lm_os <- surv_A_lm_os |>
  left_join(lg_trae_occ, by = "id") |>
  mutate(lg_trae = replace_na(lg_trae, 0L),
         group   = factor(lg_trae, levels=c(0,1), labels=c("No LG TrAE","LG TrAE")))

df_A_lg_lm_pfs <- surv_A_lm_pfs |>
  left_join(lg_trae_occ, by = "id") |>
  mutate(lg_trae = replace_na(lg_trae, 0L),
         group   = factor(lg_trae, levels=c(0,1), labels=c("No LG TrAE","LG TrAE")))

# Original
fit_pfs_orig <- survfit(Surv(pfs_time_mo, pfs_event) ~ group, data = df_A_lg)
sd_pfs_orig  <- survdiff(Surv(pfs_time_mo, pfs_event) ~ group, data = df_A_lg)
fit_os_orig  <- survfit(Surv(os_time_mo,  os_event)  ~ group, data = df_A_lg)
sd_os_orig   <- survdiff(Surv(os_time_mo,  os_event)  ~ group, data = df_A_lg)
s_pfs_orig <- km_stats(fit_pfs_orig, sd_pfs_orig)
s_os_orig  <- km_stats(fit_os_orig,  sd_os_orig)

# Landmark
fit_pfs_lm <- survfit(Surv(pfs_time_lm, pfs_event) ~ group, data = df_A_lg_lm_pfs)
sd_pfs_lm  <- survdiff(Surv(pfs_time_lm, pfs_event) ~ group, data = df_A_lg_lm_pfs)
fit_os_lm  <- survfit(Surv(os_time_lm,  os_event)  ~ group, data = df_A_lg_lm_os)
sd_os_lm   <- survdiff(Surv(os_time_lm,  os_event)  ~ group, data = df_A_lg_lm_os)
s_pfs_lm <- km_stats(fit_pfs_lm, sd_pfs_lm)
s_os_lm  <- km_stats(fit_os_lm,  sd_os_lm)

Figure 3A — 24-Biomarker Cox Forest (landmark)

Show code 
bio24_A      <- build_bio24(ae_early_A, surv_A)
cox_A_orig   <- cox_forest_orig(bio24_A, surv_A)
cox_A_lm     <- cox_forest_lm(bio24_A, surv_A)

Discussion §4.1 — Fisher Test: LG TrAE × HG AE Overlap (landmark)

The paper (§4.1) tests whether the low-grade TrAE and high-grade AE biomarkers are independent using a Fisher exact test. The landmark analysis affects this test directly: 4 of the 9 HG AE patients had pfs_time ≤ 30 days and are excluded at the landmark, leaving very few HG AE patients and making the test severely underpowered.

The paper also contains a numerical error in this passage: the stated count of “six” patients with HG AE in the LG TrAE group (n = 22) is inconsistent with both the stated percentage (6/22 = 27% ≠ 14%) and Figure S3 (total HG AE = 9; 6 + 6 = 12 ≠ 9). The correct count is three (3/22 = 13.6% ≈ 14%, giving 6 + 3 = 9 ✓).

Show code 
# AE biomarker flags
lg_trae_flag <- ae_early_A |> filter(trae, low_grade)  |> distinct(id) |> mutate(lg=1L)
hg_any_flag  <- ae_early_A |> filter(high_grade)        |> distinct(id) |> mutate(hg=1L)

df_fisher <- surv_A |>
  left_join(lg_trae_flag, by="id") |> mutate(lg=replace_na(lg,0L)) |>
  left_join(hg_any_flag,  by="id") |> mutate(hg=replace_na(hg,0L))

df_fisher_lm <- df_fisher |> filter(pfs_time > LM_DAYS)

# Full cohort

ft_orig  <- fisher.test(tab_orig)

# Landmark
tab_lm <- table(LG_TrAE=df_fisher_lm$lg, HG_AE=df_fisher_lm$hg)
ft_lm  <- fisher.test(tab_lm)

WarningPaper §4.1 — compound error and its implications

The paper concludes p = 0.12 (not significant) and infers that “early low-grade overall TrAE maintains unique predictive value even under mild association with high-grade overall AE.” This conclusion rests on an erroneous count.

With the correct count of three (not six) in the LG TrAE group, the Fisher exact test gives p = 0.0126 — significant at α = 0.05. This means the two biomarker groups are associated: patients without early LG TrAE are significantly more likely to have early HG AE (60% vs. 14%). The conclusion of “mild association” and “unique predictive value” is not supported by the corrected data.

At the day-30 PFS landmark, 4 of the 9 HG AE patients are excluded (all had pfs_time ≤ 30 days), reducing the HG AE group to only 5 patients. The test becomes underpowered (p = 0.3031) and no conclusion about independence can be drawn.

      p_os_orig<0.05 & p_os_lm<0.05 ~ "✓ both",
      p_os_orig<0.05 & p_os_lm>=0.05 ~ "⚠ lost",
      p_os_orig>=0.05 & p_os_lm<0.05 ~ "⚠ gained",
      TRUE ~ "✗ ns both"),
    `PFS orig p`= round(p_pfs_orig,3),
    `PFS lm p`  = round(p_pfs_lm,3),
    `PFS sig?`  = case_when(
      p_pfs_orig<0.05 & p_pfs_lm<0.05 ~ "✓ both",
      p_pfs_orig<0.05 & p_pfs_lm>=0.05 ~ "⚠ lost",
      p_pfs_orig>=0.05 & p_pfs_lm<0.05 ~ "⚠ gained",
      TRUE ~ "✗ ns both")) |>
  knitr::kable()

NoteInterpretation notes

Guarantee-time (immortal-time) bias arises when the AE biomarker window and the survival window overlap: patients who die before day 30 cannot have been classified as “AE-positive,” regardless of their biology. The landmark at day 30 removes this overlap.

What to look for: - If significance is lost at the landmark for “AE-positive → better survival” associations (e.g., LG TrAE, LG overall AE), that suggests the original result was partly driven by early deaths populating the “no AE” group — a form of guarantee-time bias. - If significance is retained at the landmark, the association extends beyond the early period and is not purely a guarantee-time artefact. - For “AE-positive → poorer survival” associations (HG AE), the landmark provides a check in the opposite direction: patients with HG AE who die very quickly (within 30 days) would be excluded, which would tend to weaken the association. Retention of significance confirms the adverse prognosis signal in patients who survive the initial window.

Limitation of this landmark: Excluding patients who die or progress within 30 days reduces statistical power, especially in small cohorts (n = 32 and n = 50). Some nominal changes in significance (e.g., p moving from 0.03 to 0.07) may reflect reduced power rather than a true absence of the association.

Cohort B mechanism: The “no LG AE” group in Cohort B contained only 4 patients. Two of them (pfs_time = 11 days, os_time = 11/17 days) are excluded by the PFS landmark, leaving only 2 patients in that group — insufficient to sustain any statistical comparison. The original signal was substantially driven by these two very early deaths.

Alternative Bias-Correction: Time-Varying Covariate Cox Model

A time-varying covariate (TVC) Cox model is an alternative to the hard landmark exclusion. Rather than discarding patients who die before day 30, it treats the AE biomarker as a covariate that is “revealed” at day 30: all patients contribute to the risk set from time 0 with ae = 0 (status not yet known), and from day 30 onward with their actual AE status. This avoids excluding anyone while still preventing the guarantee-time bias.

Counting process formulation. For each patient with event time \(T\):

  • Segment 1: \((0, \min(T, 30\text{ days}))\), ae_status = 0, event = 1 only if \(T \le 30\)
  • Segment 2: \((\text{day 30}, T)\), ae_status = actual, event = original — only for patients with \(T > 30\)
Show code 
make_tvc <- function(surv_df, ae_flag_col, time_col, event_col, lm_mo = LM_MO) {
  d <- surv_df |> rename(T = !!time_col, ev = !!event_col, ae = !!ae_flag_col)
  seg1 <- d |> transmute(
    id, ae_status = 0L,
    tstart = 0,
    tstop  = pmin(T, lm_mo),
    event  = if_else(T <= lm_mo, ev, 0L))
  seg2 <- d |> filter(T > lm_mo) |> transmute(
    id, ae_status = ae,
    tstart = lm_mo,
    tstop  = T,
    event  = ev)
  bind_rows(seg1, seg2) |> arrange(id, tstart)
}

TVC vs Landmark vs Original: main biomarkers

Show code 
## AE occurrence flag tables
ae_A_lg    <- ae_early_A |> filter(trae, low_grade) |> distinct(id) |> mutate(ae=1L)
ae_A_hg    <- ae_early_A |> filter(high_grade)      |> distinct(id) |> mutate(ae=1L)
ae_B_lg    <- ae_early_B |> filter(low_grade)        |> distinct(id) |> mutate(ae=1L)
ae_B_hg    <- ae_early_B |> filter(high_grade)       |> distinct(id) |> mutate(ae=1L)
ae_B_lgtrae<- ae_early_B |> filter(low_grade, trae)  |> distinct(id) |> mutate(ae=1L)

## Helper: one-row tibble with orig, landmark, and TVC Cox results
one_row <- function(cohort, bm, endpoint, sv, ae_ids, t_mo, t_days, ev) {
  d    <- sv |> left_join(ae_ids, by="id") |> mutate(ae=replace_na(ae,0L))
  # Original
  fo   <- as.formula(paste0("Surv(",t_mo,",",ev,") ~ ae"))
  cxo  <- coxph(fo, data=d); so <- summary(cxo)$coefficients
  # Landmark (shift time, restrict)
  d_lm <- d |> filter(.data[[t_days]] > LM_DAYS) |>
    mutate(t_lm = .data[[t_mo]] - LM_MO)
  cxl  <- tryCatch(
    coxph(Surv(t_lm, .data[[ev]]) ~ ae, data=d_lm),
    error=\(e) NULL)
  sl   <- if (!is.null(cxl)) summary(cxl)$coefficients else NULL
  # TVC
  d_tvc <- make_tvc(d, "ae", t_mo, ev)
  cxt   <- coxph(Surv(tstart, tstop, event) ~ ae_status, data=d_tvc)
  st    <- summary(cxt)$coefficients
  tibble(
    Cohort=cohort, Biomarker=bm, Endpoint=endpoint,
    n_total=nrow(d), n_lm=nrow(d_lm),
    HR_orig=round(exp(so[1,1]),3),  p_orig=round(so[1,5],4),
    HR_lm  =if(!is.null(sl)) round(exp(sl[1,1]),3) else NA_real_,
    p_lm   =if(!is.null(sl)) round(sl[1,5],4)      else NA_real_,
    HR_tvc =round(exp(st[1,1]),3),  p_tvc =round(st[1,5],4))
}

sig_fmt <- function(p) if_else(is.na(p), "-", if_else(p < 0.05, paste0("**✓** p=", formatC(p,"f",4)), paste0("p=", formatC(p,"f",4))))

    `LM HR`   = HR_lm,   `LM result`  = sig_fmt(p_lm),

ImportantKey finding: TVC ≡ Landmark for binary AE occurrence biomarkers

The time-varying covariate model produces identical HR and p-values to the landmark Cox model. This is mathematically expected: in the pre-landmark segment (0 to day 30), all patients have ae_status = 0 — there is zero variation in the predictor, so the segment contributes no information to the partial likelihood. The full partial likelihood reduces to the post-landmark likelihood alone, which is exactly what the landmark Cox model estimates.

Consequence. For binary AE occurrence biomarkers, the TVC and landmark analyses are equivalent. The guarantee-time correction conclusions are therefore the same regardless of which method is used:

  • Cohort A — LG TrAE OS and HG AE OS/PFS associations remain significant after correction (p = 0.011 and p = 0.001/0.021). LG TrAE PFS is borderline (p = 0.054), likely reflecting reduced power with 5 patients excluded.
  • Cohort B — LG AE OS/PFS associations do not survive correction (p ≈ 0.33–0.45). The HG AE OS association also loses significance (p = 0.28). The primary driver: 2 of 4 “no LG AE” patients in Cohort B died within 11–17 days, disproportionately anchoring the “no AE, poor outcome” arm. Once the guarantee-time is removed, the remaining 2 “no AE” patients (pfs_time = 56 and 112 days) do not differ meaningfully from the LG AE group.

For continuous biomarkers (frequency, duration summed over the window), the TVC and landmark analyses would no longer be equivalent, since continuous values can vary within the pre-landmark window. All 24-biomarker analyses using non-occurrence measures (fuq, fall, dur) are beyond this analysis and would need a properly specified TVC using intermediate measurement values.

TipSummary: which results are robust to guarantee-time correction?
Cohort Association Orig sig? After correction Verdict
A LG TrAE → better OS ✓ p=0.007 ✓ p=0.011 Robust
A LG TrAE → better PFS ✓ p=0.002 ⚠ p=0.054 Borderline (5 excluded, n=27)
A HG AE → worse OS ✓ p=0.0002 ✓ p=0.001 Robust
A HG AE → worse PFS ✓ p=0.0003 ✓ p=0.021 Robust
B LG AE → better OS ✓ p=0.031 ✗ p=0.45 Not robust — guarantee-time bias
B LG AE → better PFS ✓ p=0.022 ✗ p=0.33 Not robust — guarantee-time bias
B HG AE → worse OS ✓ p=0.024 ✗ p=0.28 Not robust (HG AE n small)
